gaps.wanted: The rack depth the bracket kits span. The guide's Figure 29 and its table name the 19-inch brackets ACC-KIT-T1=, the four-point extension rails and five brackets 4PT-KIT-T2=, and the 23-inch, 24-inch and ETSI brackets RACK-KIT-T1=, and print no range of rack depth, no setback and no part dimension. A kind: kit contract needs a depth or a factory preset, so no kit is written and chassis.kits is left out; the three positions above are named without a number.
Whether the front USB Type A storage port is USB 2.0 or 3.0. The guide says only "USB Type A storage port".
The faces of C9300-NM-2Q, C9300-NM-4G, C9300-NM-4M, C9300-NM-2Y and C9300-NM-8X. The guide draws them isometrically and prints no dimension. Left for the next 9300 batch.
The pictograms under the status lamps and beside the mini-USB port. The guide's Figure 8 gives their names and the NetBox elevation draws them at a few pixels each; no legend is drawn.
A flat drawing of the lid, the underside and the sides. The guide's Figure 1 and Figure 10 show them isometrically with a vent on the side and labels on the lid.

a `power-draw-max-w` on each module this chassis accepts, from the vendor's own per-card table - Cisco publishes one per ambient, most vendors publish none, and until they land a module total is a floor

an `attrs.performance` section; `cpu`, `memory` in a missing `attrs.platform` section; one of `power-max-w`, `power-max-ac-w`, `power-max-dc-w` in `attrs.power` (profile `networking` - see spec/schemas/profiles.yaml) - unlocks the About panel, and comparison against other devices
`physical-context` on 6 bays (front 1, rear 5); `physical-context` on port group rj45 - unlocks ENTITY-MIB / Redfish correlation and monitoring overlays

airflow.note: The Fan Module section: "The airflow direction is from front-to-rear and side-to-rear." One airflow for every build, so there are no airflow configurations.

colour.note: #cccccc, the median of the pale bar between the two jack rows in the NetBox front elevation.

console-over-management.note: The guide's Ethernet Management Port text says the switch is reached "through the 10/100/1000 Ethernet management port or one of the console ports" and the RJ-45 Console Port LED table says the RJ-45 console is disabled while the USB console is active, so the front mini-USB and the rear RJ-45 are one console, and the management port is its own.

front-scale.note: EVERY FRONT POSITION IS READ OFF THE NETBOX ELEVATION, NOT THE GUIDE'S FIGURE 1, WHICH IS ISOMETRIC. The elevation is 2289 px wide for the 482.6 mm rack face, 4.743 px per mm, and the body is taken to be centred between the ears with the guide's 444.5 mm, starting at 90.3 px. The jack cavities measure 60 px (12.6 mm) across and 31 px (6.5 mm) down on a 67.3 px (14.19 mm) column step and a 66.5 px (14.0 mm) row step; the rows centre 15.27 and 29.3 mm below the body's top edge, which sits 4.1 px under the picture's. Good to about a millimetre.

left-cluster.note: The beacon button (Figure 1 callout 1, "Beacon LED (UID button)", a lit square), the maker's mark, the Mode button, the status lamps, the USB mini-Type B console port (callout 3) and the USB Type A storage port (callout 4) are read off the NetBox elevation at the scale of front-scale. The guide's Figure 8 names the lamps in two rows, Status, Duplex, Speed, Stack and PoE above, then System, Active, XPS and S-PWR, and the Console lamp beside the mini-USB port; the metal prints pictograms and not words, so no legend is drawn and each lamp is named by its id. The lamp positions are the pictograms' centres. THE FRONT USB TYPE A PORT'S GENERATION IS NOT STATED: the rear port is "USB3.0-SSD" and the front is only "USB Type A storage port", so it is drawn with the 2.0 tongue.

network-module-bay.note: Figure 1 callout 6, "Network module slots". The bay is read off the NetBox elevation, which draws a C9300-NM-8X seated: 364.8 to 440.8 mm across and 42.5 mm high, 4.3 mm beyond the last block. The guide's Table 5 and the Installing a Network Module chapter say the blank C9300-NM-BLANK is fitted "when the switch has no uplink ports (this is required for sufficient air flow)". The blank is the default. THE NETWORK MODULES THEMSELVES, C9300-NM-2Q, -4G, -4M, -2Y and -8X (and the C9300X modules the C9300X switches take), ARE NOT MODELLED here and are left for the next 9300 batch; the bay accepts only the blank until they are.

numbering.note: The legends under the strip are the NetBox elevation's: 01X and 12X, 13X and 24X, 25X and 36X, 37X and 48X, one pair at the ends of each block. The elevation prints 01X with a leading zero; it is carried as drawn. Port numbering is as printed, and the interface names (Cisco's GigabitEthernet1/0/1 to 1/0/48, which the community NetBox file gives for this model and the guide does not print for the downlinks) are not on the metal and are left out.

port-lamps.note: One lamp per port in a strip along the bottom edge, an up triangle for the odd (upper) port and a down triangle for the even, as the elevation draws them and the 4948E's lamps are. THE ELEVATION DRAWS SEVEN PAIRS OF TRIANGLES ACROSS EACH BLOCK OF SIX COLUMNS, at an 11.7 mm step, which cannot be one lamp per port. The pairs are placed under their own columns, the two triangles 5.17 mm apart as the elevation draws them, and the strip's height is its 40.5 mm below the top. The meaning of each colour is the guide's Table 15 (green link, blinking green activity, amber blocked) and the mode decides which Table 14 reading the lamps show.

ports.note: 24 columns of two jacks in four blocks of six, numbered DOWN each column (odd on the top row, even beneath) as the 4948E's blocks are; the NetBox elevation prints 01X to 12X, 13X to 24X, 25X to 36X and 37X to 48X under the four blocks. The column step is 14.19 mm and a block starts 89.4 mm after the last, a 4.26 mm gutter on the cell pitch, which predicts the fourth block's last column to 0.1 mm. THE ELEVATION'S JACK PITCH IS 14.19 AND NOT THE REGISTRY'S 13.97: the 1.5 percent difference is the elevation's scale or the registry's note, and the elevation's own value is kept so that the blocks land on the artwork. The jack cell is the registry's 12.7 x 11.0.

power.note: Table 18 and the front panel text: PoE budget 437 W with one 715 W supply, "Available PoE" of the C9300-48P. The guide holds no table of the switch's own draw, and none is written.

rack-positions.note: Figures 32 to 35 of the guide draw the front-mounting, mid-mounting, rear-mounting and four-point mounting positions, isometrically, with no dimension. Front-mounting is the first and the guide's Mounting the Switch in a Rack step 1 attaches the brackets for "the front or rear mounting positions"; it is taken as the shipped default. No setback is printed and none is written.

rear-fans.note: Three FAN-T2 modules (the guide: "support three internal hot-swappable 12-V fan modules (FAN-T2=)") at a 63.0 mm step, each 43.9 x 41.1 by Table 48, centred 70.5, 133.5 and 196.5 mm from the left. The elevation draws each opening 39.1 wide and the 43.9 is the guide's. The StackWise-480 carriers lie between them (92.5 to 111.1 and 156.2 to 174.8 mm) and hold three stacked connectors each, as the elevation draws them, at a 9.3 mm pitch; the guide's Figure 10 points at two ports in all, so each carrier is one port.

rear-left.note: The ground connectors (callout 1) as two ground screws, the USB 3.0 SSD slot (callout 2) under a cover the guide calls the "blank cover on the USB 3.0 SSD slot", the RJ-45 CONSOLE port (callout 4) on the left and the RJ-45 MGMT port (callout 5) on the right, each 14.2 mm from the next, and the lamps for the console and the beacon (callout 3) in the icon row beneath. The jacks' keyways point down.

rear-power.note: The StackPower connectors (callout 7), S-PWR 1 over S-PWR 2, with XPS under the first, at 233.0 mm, and the two supply bays 258.5 and 348.4 mm from the left, each the supplies' 82.55 x 40.1 by the guide's physical table and the elevation's 81.9 measured. A 13.5 mm strip of bare chassis closes the right. The guide does not number the supply slots; psu-1 is the left.

rear-scale.note: Every rear position is read off the NetBox elevation of the C9300-48T, 2428 px wide for 482.6 mm, 5.031 px per mm, the body 444.5 mm from 95.8 px. NETBOX'S C9300-48P REAR IS BYTE-IDENTICAL TO THE C9300-48U'S (COVERAGE.md item 30) AND SO IS NOT USED; the 48T rear is, which agrees with Figure 10 in its order from the left: ground connectors, SSD slot, console and management ports, fan, StackWise, fan, StackWise, fan, StackPower, two supplies. It labels its supplies PWR-C1-1100WAC and draws them as the dark honeycomb faces the components use.

Table 42 (dimensions), Table 43 (weight), Table 18 (default supply and PoE), Table 35 (the supplies), Figures 1, 8 and 10 (the front, the lamps and the rear), the Fan Module section and Table 48. COMMUNITY NETBOX DEVICETYPE-LIBRARY ELEVATIONS (cisco-c9300-48p.front.png 2289 x 219 and cisco-c9300-48t.rear.png 2428 x 234) are a second opinion and the only flat drawings held, not Cisco's. No data sheet, no photograph, no 3D model and no stencil is held for the Catalyst 9300.

the-envelope.note: Table 42: 1.73 x 17.5 x 19.2 in (4.4 x 44.5 x 48.8 cm), with the fan modules and the default supplies installed. Width 444.5 (17.5 in; the 44.5 cm agrees). Depth 487.7 (19.2 in; 48.8 cm is 488). HEIGHT 44.45, THE RACK UNIT, NOT THE PRINTED 1.73 IN (43.9 mm): the guide prints 1.73 in for every 1RU model and both are nominal, so the unit is carried and the printed height is one millimetre under it. The 17.5 in is the body between the ear fold lines (the NetBox elevation draws ears outside it).

the-licence-suffix.note: C9300-48P-A (Network Advantage) and C9300-48P-E (Network Essentials) differ in software licence only; the guide lists the hardware as C9300-48P throughout. One device, and the suffixed ordering codes are not part numbers of a configuration.

the-rear-figure.note: THE TASK'S "C9300 REAR PANEL ON PDF PAGE 41" IS FIGURE 14, THE CATALYST 9300X. Figure 10 of the guide, "Rear Panel of a Cisco Catalyst 9300 Series Switch" (PDF page 39), is isometric and the guide holds no flat drawing of the C9300 rear. Its callouts name, in order, the ground connectors, the USB 3.0 SSD port, the BEACON LED, the RJ-45 CONSOLE port, the RJ-45 MGMT port, the fan modules, the StackPower connectors, the AC OK and PS OK lamps, the StackWise-480 port connectors and the power supply modules.
